highlights.title: Sharing dangerous driving videos is 'truly reprehensible', PM says
highlights.summary: His comments come as the government urged TikTok and other social media firms to remove wrong-way driving videos.
body: The government has urged social media companies to remove posts celebrating dangerous driving, as Prime Minister Andy Burnham branded sharing them "truly reprehensible".
Earlier Defence Minister Luke Pollard told BBC Breakfast that "social media companies could take the content down easily and adjust their algorithms to stop it being distributed".
Two police officers died when a car going the wrong way down a dual carriageway crashed into their vehicle near Middlesbrough on Saturday. Five passengers in the other car were also killed.
A TikTok account believed to belong to one of the five passengers, 18-year-old Makai Saddington, previously shared videos appearing to show dangerous driving, which have since been removed.

highlights.title: How to encourage smarter AI use in the classroom
highlights.summary: This article is from Making AI Work, MIT Technology Review’s limited-run newsletter examining how to apply LLMs across industries. To receive it in your inbox, sign up here. Chatbots took many schools by surprise upon their release a few years ago.
body: Nevertheless, the generative AI boom increased the burden on teachers, who were already working long hours to plan lessons, make homework assignments, and grade exams, and now needed to adapt to a new technology. For many, it still feels like there’s no clear path forward. Organizations ranging from OpenAI to UNESCO encourage AI use in the classroom, but many teachers feel confused about how exactly to handle it.

Cheshire Academy is a private boarding and day school in Connecticut with about 400 students in grades 9 through 12. Administrators there don’t force instructors to use AI at all, though the school’s librarian and technology coordinator George Aiello claims the “vast majority” of instructors use it in some way. The educators there are trying a patchwork of programs, including general-purpose chatbots like ChatGPT and Perplexity as well as more specialized tools like MagicSchool, an AI-powered platform meant specifically for educators.

highlights.title: “How did we misjudge this so badly…?” What Supercell learned from upsetting Clash Royale players
highlights.summary: Game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell talked through Clash Royale player drama and how to deal with it at Gamescom Dev.
body: Supercell explained some of the thinking behind several major Clash Royale updates that caused community uproar today at Gamescom Dev.
Playing on some of the more extreme feedback the Clash Royale team has received recently, game design lead James Back declared: “At the end of last year, we killed Clash Royale”.
He also admitted that, after several months of fierce, negative player reaction, Back sat at his desk wondering: “How did we misjudge this so badly? Like, how did we get this quite so wrong…?”
Game design lead Back and community manager Emilia Russell then talked through some of the game updates that caused the player discontent, and what they learned from it all.

highlights.title: F1 in the Netherlands: The driver you most want to beat is your teammate
highlights.summary: After months of rumors surrounding his future, now we know: Four-time champion Max Verstappen is staying in the sport for the foreseeable future. The news broke on the eve of the Dutch Grand Prix, held this past weekend at Zandvoort in the Netherlands as F1 returned from its mandatory summer…
body: Verstappen’s wasn’t the only contract news—Williams will keep both Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz, too. More than once I’ve noticed a driver having an underwhelming weekend following a freshly signed contract; in this case, all three had a weekend they’d probably rather forget. They weren’t the only ones, though. Up and down the grid, we saw friction between teammates. And there’s no one an F1 driver wants to beat more than the only other person to have the same car as they do.
Formula 1 returned from its summer break with this weekend’s Dutch Grand Prix.

One of the things that sets F1 apart from most other disciplines in motorsport is the constant in-season development of the cars. A team might start the year with the best car and a commanding advantage over its rivals, but others can and will catch up. The 2009 season is a good example of this; Brawn GP started the year with at least a second a lap in hand over the rest of the grid, and Jenson Button built up a big early lead in the championship after winning five of the first six races.

highlights.title: Valor, Point72 back General Intuition at $6B valuation as AI startup pushes into robotics
highlights.summary: General Intuition, the startup building a foundation model that trains generalized AI agents how to move through space and time, is in talks to raise at a $6 billion pre-money valuation from new investors including Valor Ventures, Point72 Ventures, and Seven Seven Six.
body: Existing investors including Khosla Ventures and General Catalyst are also participating in the round. The fresh funds would come just weeks after General Intuition raised $320 million at a $2.3 billion valuation.
The news confirms earlier reporting on the deal for what is becoming one of the hottest startups tackling physical AI.

CEO Pim de Witte spun out General Intuition last October from his video game clip-sharing platform Medal, using its hundreds of millions of hours of gameplay and “action labels” — records of which buttons a player pressed and when — as an initial dataset.

Investor Vinod Khosla recently told TechCrunch that he believes those action labels will be a key part of the “emergence of intuition,” or the ability for a model to truly generalize across tasks that it wasn’t explicitly trained on.

highlights.title: Is Norris now Antonelli's biggest title threat?
highlights.summary: While he won neither of the race formats across the Zandvoort Sprint weekend, Kimi Antonelli increased his overall world championship lead at the Dutch Grand Prix as Formula 1 returned from its summer break.
body: The Mercedes driver now leads both team-mate George Russell and Ferrari rival Lewis Hamilton by 59 points, the second-largest advantage Antonelli has enjoyed at the top of the Drivers' Championship so far this season.

But Antonelli's advantage over the driver now occupying fourth place in the standings was cut by a further eight points, following reigning champion Lando Norris' second successive Grand Prix victory, which moved him to within 83 points of the championship lead.

Norris became just the second driver after Antonelli to claim consecutive wins this season, with the McLaren driver's Zandvoort triumph coming after he overtook the championship leader on track. Antonelli had initially reclaimed the lead from Norris at the restart following the red flag triggered by Max Verstappen's heavy lap-one crash.
Yet does the result mean that Norris' hopes of retaining his world title, which seemed all-but over just a few races ago before McLaren brought a notable car upgrade to Budapest, are firmly back on?

highlights.title: Vampire Survivors Gets Bloodier and Raunchier In This Wild New Game
highlights.summary: Blood Dungeon is a chaotic riff on Vampire Survivors that trades in depth for high-score chasing buffoonery.
body: Here’s a two-word video game review for you: Blood Dungeon. That’s it. That’s the review.

No, really, what more do you need me to say? It’s a video game called Blood Dungeon. Bless developer Messhof, the studio behind Nidhogg and Wheel World, for giving its latest game a title that tells you exactly what you’re getting with this lo-fi Vampire Survivors riff upfront. It’s like seeing a store-brand cereal called Sugar Balls. No confusion about what’s in that box! As it says on the tin, Blood Dungeon is about as lowbrow as video games get — and that’s exactly what I ordered. It’s a proudly crude roguelike built for a generation raised on Adult Swim. Sometimes, you just crave something that dares to be stupid.

highlights.title: “We killed Clash Royale!”: What Supercell learned from failed updates
highlights.summary: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates. During a session at Gamescom Dev titled 'Clash Royale: Lessons from the players', Supercell game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell shared their insights from…
body: Russell noted, though, that even the harshest and most critical feedback comes from a place of caring about a game and players wanting the best for it - even if it’s not always given in the most clear or constructive way.

First, they opened up on the Season Shop. Described as “one of the most popular reward systems in the game”, it allowed players to spend Season Tokens on cards and other items. In March 2025, Supercell decided to remove it.

Back said it was for good reason. The team felt it only benefitted a small group of core players and they wanted to put the rewards somewhere more accessible to more players. The update worked at achieving that goal. The percentage of monthly active users earning any common wild cards grew from 59.8% in March 2025 to 67.4% in April 2025.
But due to the Season Shop’s popularity, its sudden removal resulted in “broken trust” and negative sentiment. The average daily rating on Google Play plummeted.
points: Clash Royale has had its ups and downs over the years with some major backlash from players and fans over updates.

highlights.title: A job that changed me: I worked for an infamous clothing brand – but it was one of the most positive workplaces of my life
highlights.summary: Despite its global reputation, my time there felt less sexy party, more wholesome summer camp. Then one day my boss told me a hard truth. When I tell people I spent a chunk of my early 20s working at a hipster clothing retailer infamous for salacious ads and sexual assault allegations, I’m usually…
body: But the truth is, despite the global reputation, our little store in Melbourne was one of the most positive workplaces of my life.

The store was divided into two tribes: shop assistants – mostly doe-eyed art girls – and backstock workers – mostly charming burnout skaters. While the shop assistants got the most attention and lustful public glares, the weed-scented heart of the store was the backstock room.
I was a rare breed: a shop assistant who transitioned to a backstock role, mostly because I couldn’t use a cash register properly.

Despite technically being a demotion, the move made me the envy of the shop assistants. In backstock we’d listen to music while folding T-shirts and debating Simpsons lore like greasy-haired scholars.

highlights.title: They Dedicated Their Lives to Teaching. Then the Deepfakes Started
highlights.summary: The deepfake epidemic in schools is affecting more than students. Four teachers tell WIRED about becoming targets of sexualized, AI-generated content—and how difficult it was to find accountability.
body: For Luis DeSantiago, a substitute teacher in Los Banos, California, it started with a few text messages. On March 12, as he was working his other part-time job at a coffee shop, his phone lit up. A fellow barista said there was an AI photo circulating on social media. Her cousin wanted to know if it was DeSantiago.
At first, DeSantiago wasn’t worried—he figured that inappropriate photos violated TikTok’s community guidelines and were usually quickly removed.

“When I finally saw the image, that’s when it felt like a punch to the gut,” DeSantiago tells WIRED. Parts of it resembled a mirror selfie that he remembered taking at a job in college. But instead of his work uniform, he was wearing lingerie. And instead of standing normally, as he had been in the original photo, he was posing suggestively.
The texts kicked off a monthslong saga that crossed two schools and involved students and administrators. And DeSantiago is far from the only educator who’s been victimized this way.

highlights.title: New D&D Book Gives Every Class More Magic and Pets to Play With
highlights.summary: After the “new era” of Dungeons & Dragons kicked off with Ravenloft: The Horrors Within, Wizards of the Coast has a very different type of product lined up to follow the latest excursion into the dreaded mists of its horror setting.
body: Polygon had the chance to read and review both products early, and together they reaffirm the current design philosophy of 2024’s 5.5 edition of the game. Arcana Unleashed goes a long way toward fixing some subclasses that were lackluster in 5e, and it gives more magic-focused options to players. In the process, it also erodes the barriers between classes, offering more flexibility for each class at the expense of what makes each distinct to begin with. Whether you like it or not, that’s D&D’s current direction.

Of course, this being a book about magic, wizard subclasses are treated with extreme care. Players now get all the magic school options that were missing from the Player’s Handbook, namely Conjurer, Necromancer, Enchanter, and Transmuter. They all receive significant boosts compared to their 5e versions. The Conjurer now gets their teleportation ability at level 3 rather than 6, and for a number of times equal to their Intelligence modifier, making this wizard very hard to catch on the battlefield. At level 6, the Conjurer’s summoned creatures become stronger, with temporary hit points and resistance to most forms of damage.

highlights.title: Trump tried to curb clean energy. It’s booming anyway.
highlights.summary: Donald Trump is presiding over an unexpected clean energy boom, as rising electricity demand spurs investment in new capacity despite the US administration’s efforts to thwart a solar and wind rollout.
body: Clean energy additions will rise by a record 45 gigawatts this year, according to S&P Global Energy—equivalent to the average electricity demand of Turkey. The increase is roughly 25 percent higher than the record set in 2024.

The US president’s war in Iran, which has driven up global energy prices, along with surging power demand from AI data centers and developers’ rush to capitalize on expiring tax credits, are driving the cleantech boom, said analysts. Trump’s administration has also been pragmatic in the face of its energy needs.

“There was a campaign promise to go against renewables, but at the same time they’re realizing that you can’t do without it,” said Izzet Bensusan, chief executive of Captona, an energy infrastructure investment group. “I don’t see a world where power demand is flattening out.”
S&P said new solar and wind capacity will jump in 2026 by nearly a third and almost 50 percent respectively. Solar will set another record in 2027, while wind falls back before recovering.

body: “The progress recently has been amazing,” Michael C. Frank, a cognitive scientist at Stanford University, says of LLMs. “But we still have to burn down a forest and scrape the entire sum of all human knowledge to re-create this milestone that happens in our living rooms over the course of a year.”

This yawning divide between children and machines is called the data efficiency gap. And it raises a tantalizing question for cognitive scientists and a challenge for the architects of AI models: How is it that kids can still outperform the most linguistically sophisticated machines ever built?

body: Idiots, the new comedy starring Dave Franco, O’Shea Jackson Jr., Mason Thames, and Kiernan Shipka, has a little bit of everything: a star-studded cast, a bone-chilling villainous turn, and Dave Franco performing in what he calls a “top three ‘shit yourself’ scene in cinematic history.”

The upcoming movie, written and directed by Macon Blair (The Toxic Avenger, I Don’t Feel At Home in This World Anymore), tells the story of what happens “when two unqualified bozos (Franco, Jackson) are hired to transfer a rich teen (Thames) to rehab [and] their straightforward gig quickly spirals into dangerous mayhem.”

I sat down with Blair and the cast for an exclusive roundtable interview to unpack all of the movie’s big moments (many comedic, some filled with drama verging on horror) and dive into the challenges of bringing an ambitious story with a stacked cast to the big screen on a limited budget.

One of the biggest hurdles Blair encountered when making Idiots was what exactly to call it. The film was originally titled (and marketed as) The Shitheads. Blair says that, despite what you might think, it wasn’t outside pressure that forced the name change.

highlights.title: ‘Standard’ velvet hangers? There’s nothing standard about some of the items on John Lewis’s uni essentials list| Emma Beddington
highlights.summary: It used to be that dorm rooms were chaotically messy. Does this new generation really need an £80 spice rack and velvet clothes hangers? Of all the questions this year’s freshers may be nervously asking themselves as they prepare for this next phase – did I pick the right course?
body: Fret no longer, enquiring young minds: John Lewis has the answer on its packing checklist for students. Thirty to 40, it claims, wildly, “consisting mostly of standard velvet or plastic hangers”. “Standard” velvet? I missed this memo.

I found the list via the student news site the Tab, which posted a TikTok mocking J-Lew’s notions of what constitute “essentials”: a £495 Marc Jacobs bag, a £399 desk and an £80 spice rack carousel (I also spotted a £185 Ralph Lauren quarter-zip for those must-attend “man in finance” costume parties).

In fairness, most of the stuff on there is fine, but the Stanley cups and shower squeegees conjure a slightly dispiriting picture of wellness-focused, sensible, hygienic youth. I know that’s their generation’s reputation, but it would be nice if parents could be persuaded not to stock up, instead letting them go rogue and fill their kitchens, bathrooms and bedrooms with chaotically impractical stuff they choose themselves. Isn’t that what early adulthood is all about?

body: The third stage of the Vuelta a España ended without a winner after being halted because of hail on Monday.

Riders started taking shelter in shops and restaurants by the road with about 15km to go on the difficult 174km route from ‌Gruissan to ‌Font-Romeu that was due to finish in the French Pyrenees. Organisers neutralised the race as the peloton scaled the Col de Mont-Louis and huge hailstones began pelting the ‌riders, with ice on the road and the threat of lightning. They eventually suspended the stage and declared no winner.
“For the security of the riders, stage three has been cancelled due to hail and severe weather,” race organisers said. “There will be no winner and no podium ceremony.”

The riders started communicating and asking each other to slow down when the hail began. Mats Wenzel of Equipo Kern Pharm and Lorenzo Fortunato of XDS Astana were in a breakaway at the time the race was called off.

highlights.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Ernie the danger dog – who loves dicing with death
highlights.summary: He has chased a deer across a dual carriageway, eaten an entire tray of chocolate brownies and jumped head first into a canal. But despite all the worry he brings us, he is extraordinarily lovable.
body: Ernie found his way into our hearts and home about nine years ago, when he strategically crawled into my lap during a family visit to meet a litter of puppies. While all the other beagle puppies ran wild, Ernie sat comfortably on me with his long, soft ears dangling down. We chose him because of his placid nature and named him Ernie after my mum’s late dad, who coincidentally also had short legs and a bit of a round belly.
After a few weeks we realised that Ernie was anything but placid. His gentle temperament quickly morphed into an unruly and persistent need to find his way into danger.

The most shocking incident happened one morning in November 2022. Ernie spotted a deer in the forest behind our house. He darted away from me and my mum, through the forest and towards a busy dual carriageway. Ignoring our screams, Ernie crossed the road, missing multiple lorries and cars, making his way to safety on a small patch of grass on the pavement. It was a miracle he had managed to avoid injury.

highlights.title: OpenAI is building AI agents for everything. Will everyone use them?
highlights.summary: Inside the frontier lab’s push to bring AI agents from software engineers to the masses.
body: How much control are you willing to give an LLM over your digital life?

Getting the most value from a model means giving it the keys. For a control freak or the AI-hesitant, it seems like a lot. For Andrew Ambrosino, the lead engineer for OpenAI’s desktop app, it’s the only way to test the future, which is why that app now has access to, and control over, his inbox, his Slack account, his phone, apps like Notion and Figma, and more.

“If I’m asking it to write a document, is there a possibility that it’s going to pull from a private DM on that subject and not know that it’s not supposed to share some info? Yes,” Ambrosino told TechCrunch. “I’ll do it for the job. I will take the personal hit here and there if I have to. And I haven’t had to.”

Ambrosino works on OpenAI’s biggest bet, ChatGPT Work, which was released last month and is available on the company’s lowest subscription tier, for $20 a month. The product is intended to allow white-collar workers to field AI agents — hooking LLMs up to the digital workflows used by accountants, investors, doctors, and everyone else whose day-to-day is dominated by their computer.

highlights.title: Samsung's Absolutely Massive 57" Dual 4K Gaming Monitor Drops to the Lowest Price I've Ever Seen
highlights.summary: For a very limited time, the biggest and baddest gaming monitor you can possibly get (short of getting a TV) has dropped to its lowest price ever. Samsung via its official store is offering the massive 57" Samsung Odyssey Neo G9 Dual 4K UHD gaming monitor for $1,349.99 with free shipping.
body: The 57" Samsung Odyssey Neo G9 is one of few 57" dual 4K UHD monitors on the market, boasting an eye-watering 7680x2160 resolution, or the equivalent of two 4K UHD monitors stacked next to each other. Despite the display being so large, it has an above-average 140ppi pixel density, which is amazing considering the fact that in general the bigger the display, the lower the ppi. To put that into perspective, it's as sharp as a 32" 4K monitor. Wow.

The Odyssey Neo G9 is equipped with a Mini LED backlight paired with a quantum dot (QLED) panel. Like its namesake suggests, mini-LED panels have smaller LEDs than traditional LED LCD monitors, so you can squeeze in more lighting zones. Mini-LED monitors are also much brighter than OLED monitors, which is very important because larger monitors are generally dimmer than smaller ones to start. Local dimming combined with higher brightness improves contrast ratio and HDR and is also useful in overpowering glare and reflections.
points: For a very limited time, the biggest and baddest gaming monitor you can possibly get (short of getting a TV) has dropped to its lowest price ever.
